passages.original: πῖνε, γέρον, καὶ ζῆθι· μάτην δ’ ἄρα θεῖος Ὄμηρος τείρεσθαι πολιὴν ἐκ νεότητος ἔφη.
passages.english: Drink, old man, and live; so it was in vain, after all, that divine Homer said gray old age wears [us] down from youth onward.
passages.notes: The second line is obscure. It may mean that old age, i.e. grey hair, wears a man down, or comes upon him, after youth. It is perhaps an allusion to a Homeric phrase about old age; the precise reference was not identified.

passages.original: Εὐ γε ποιῶν, Λύσιππε γέρων, Σικυώνιε πλάστα, δείκελον Αἰσώπου στήσαο τοῦ Σαμίου
passages.english: Well done, old Lysippus, sculptor of Sicyon, in setting up a likeness of Aesop of Samos
passages.notes: The passage breaks off in mid-sentence.
